The '''2024–25 season''' was the [[List of Manchester City F.C. seasons|130th season]] in the existence of [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City Football Club]] and their 23rd consecutive season in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in England|English football]]. In addition to the [[2024–25 Premier League|domestic league]], where they were competing as four-time defending champions, Manchester City also participated in the [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2024–25 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], [[2024 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]], the revamped [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]; entering the latter for the 14th consecutive season; and the expanded [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]] as winners of the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/fifaplus/en/tournaments/mens/mundial-de-clubes/usa-2025/articles/manchester-city-club-profile-history-players-qualified|title=Manchester City: Heading to Mundial de Clubes FIFA after Champions League win|publisher=[[FIFA]]|date=6 March 2024|access-date=5 May 2024}}</ref>

City began the season by defeating [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] 7–6 on penalties after a 1–1 draw in regular time on 10 August to win the [[FA Community Shield]] for the first time since [[2019 FA Community Shield|2019]].<ref name="MM">{{Cite web |title=Man Utd vs Man City LIVE: Manuel Akanji scores winner as Man City beat Man United 7-6 on penalties in Community Shield, reaction, stats & updates |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c9wjkjyqpg4t |access-date=2024-08-10 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=2024-10-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001191553/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c9wjkjyqpg4t |url-status=live}}</ref> This turned out to be their only honour of the season. On 30 October, they were eliminated in the fourth round of the EFL Cup by [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] at their [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium|stadium]] in a 1–2 defeat, the team's first that season. This game marked the beginning of a recently unprecedented period of poor form for the team, which concluded at one win in thirteen matches, and included five consecutive losses for the first time in Pep Guardiola's managerial career and the worst run for City since the [[2005–06 Manchester City F.C. season|2005–06 season]].

On 19 February, Manchester City were eliminated from the Champions League by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], losing 3–6 on aggregate after having been beaten home and away by the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|reigning champions]] in the new knockout phase play-offs. This is the first season since [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|2012–13]] where City had failed to reach the last 16 of the competition.<ref name="RM">{{Cite web |title=Real Madrid 3-1 Manchester City (Agg 6-3): Kylian Mbappe's stunning hat-trick dumps City out |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clyne5v9j7pt |access-date=2025-02-20 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 17 May, they were beaten 1–0 by [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in the [[2025 FA Cup final|FA Cup final]], City's second consecutive cup final defeat. Palace's victory was their first-ever major title and ensured the Blues failed to claim major domestic silverware for the first time since the [[2016–17 Manchester City F.C. season|2016–17 season]].<ref name="CF">{{Cite web |title=FA Cup final 2025 LIVE: Crystal Palace vs Man City - watch TV stream, score, radio & updates |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cm23zrkn7ryt |access-date=2025-05-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> A 2–0 victory away to [[Fulham F.C|Fulham]] on the final day of the Premier League season ensured City secured third place in the standings and qualified for the following season's [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], their 15th consecutive appearance in the competition.

After the end of the season proper, the club embarked on significant transfer activity, recruiting players such as [[Rayan Aït-Nouri]], [[Tijjani Reijnders]], and [[Rayan Cherki]], before travelling to the [[United States]] for the newly expanded Club World Cup. On June 30, the Blues were beaten 4–3 [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|after extra time]] by [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] in the round of 16 after having swept their group stage opponents.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Manchester City 3-4 Al-Hilal: Pep Guardiola's men stunned in thrilling World Club Cup last-16 tie |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clynqpvg783t |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Season summary==
===Pre-season===
The club ended the previous season with the main issue being whether or not [[Pep Guardiola]] would decide to extend his contract as manager beyond the end of the 2024–25 season after nine years with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=George |date=2024-05-28 |title=Pep Guardiola given two options for next job after Man City exit |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/pep-guardiola-man-city-job-29253430 |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=Manchester Evening News |language=en |archive-date=2024-05-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240529020315/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/pep-guardiola-man-city-job-29253430 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Kevin De Bruyne]] was the only key player who would start the season in the final year of his existing contract, but there was also further speculation on the futures of [[Kyle Walker]] and [[Bernardo Silva]], as there had been in previous recent summers. Rumours also emerged that Ederson could be a target for [[Saudi Pro League]] club [[Al Nassr FC|Al Nassr]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bajkowski |first=Simon |date=2024-07-16 |title=City wait on fresh Ederson bid that could change transfer plans |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/man-city-wait-fresh-ederson-29549696 |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=Manchester Evening News |language=en |archive-date=2024-07-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240717080145/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/man-city-wait-fresh-ederson-29549696 |url-status=live}}</ref>

A total of 13 current City players were selected for squads for [[UEFA Euro 2024|Euro 2024]], the joint most alongside [[Inter Milan]], and one player was selected for the [[2024 Copa América]]. Six of those players reached the semi-finals of these competitions played in the week commencing 8 July; five of those would go on to reach the respective finals played on 14 July; and two: [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] and [[Julián Alvarez]] for [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], would celebrate as champions. Rodri was also recognised as the [[UEFA Euro 2024#Awards|Player of the Tournament]] for Euro 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=City players in Euro 2024 and Copa America squads |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/euro-2024-copa-america-squads-63852497 |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=mancity.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelsey |first=George |date=14 July 2024 |title=RODRIGO NAMED EURO 2024 PLAYER OF THE TOURNAMENT |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/rodri-euro-2024-player-of-the-tournament-man-city-63856589 |access-date=19 July 2024 |website=mancity.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=England 1-2 Spain: Euro 2024 final heartbreak for England as late Spain goal secures fourth European Championship |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cp68zzx8x4rt |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=2024-07-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240715010859/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cp68zzx8x4rt |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Argentina 1-0 Colombia: Martinez goal in extra-time secures Copa America win after Lionel Messi injury |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clwy1ljp971t |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Players who had not participated in either competition returned to the club for pre-season training on 15 July to prepare for their forthcoming pre-season tour in the [[United States]]. Spanish defender [[Sergio Gómez (footballer, born 2000)|Sergio Gómez]] had been the first senior player to be transferred, leaving the club after two seasons to join [[Real Sociedad]] on 12 July. The first transfer in was announced on 18 July when Brazilian winger [[Savinho]] joined from fellow [[City Football Group|CFG]] club [[ES Troyes AC|Troyes]], after a successful loan season at [[Girona FC|Girona]], for a reported fee of £21 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Isaac |date=2024-07-18 |title=Savio signs and Ederson exit - transfer decisions Man City can make this week |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/savio-signs-ederson-exit-phillips-29561588 |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=Manchester Evening News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-18 |title=Savio: Manchester City sign Brazil winger from Troyes until 2029 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c903dvqvgpqo |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=2024-07-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240719012201/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c903dvqvgpqo |url-status=live}}</ref>

City took a largely inexperienced squad on their pre-season tour to the US, selecting only 11 previous first team players who had not played at the Euros or Copa America.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Paul |date=19 July 2024 |title=USA Tour 2024: City's travelling squad announced |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/usa-tour-2024-travelling-squad-63856989 |access-date=4 Aug 2024 |website=mancity.com}}</ref> Their two [[Croatia national football team|Croatian]] Internationals, [[Joško Gvardiol]] and [[Mateo Kovačić]], who had returned from Germany after the group stages, joined the tour at its mid-point.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 Jul 2024 |title=Gvardiol and Kovacic to join up with City in New York |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/gvardiol-kovacic-new-york-arrival-man-city-us-tour-63857088 |access-date=4 August 2024 |website=mancity.com}}</ref> The remaining 14 players were allowed extended breaks and would join the squad after its return to the UK. However, this tour squad was able to perform well and only suffered narrow losses to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and [[AC Milan|Milan]], drew with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and beat [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] convincingly with a [[Erling Haaland|Haaland]] hat-trick. The performances of Haaland, [[Jack Grealish|Grealish]] and [[Oscar Bobb]] in particular stood out in these games with the latter demonstrating he was ready for more first-team appearances in the coming season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-04 |title=Man City 4-2 Chelsea: Erling Haaland hat-trick beats Chelsea in pre-season win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cljyyrk2ly5o |access-date=2024-08-04 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Start of the season===
In their first competitive game of the season, City won the [[2024 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] by beating fierce [[Manchester derby|rivals]] [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] 7–6 on penalties after a 1–1 draw in regular time, thus avenging the defeat to the same side in the [[2024 FA Cup final]]. United opened the scoring in the 82nd minute with a strike from [[Alejandro Garnacho]], and City equalised in the penultimate minute of normal time with a [[Bernardo Silva]] header from an excellent [[Oscar Bobb]] run and cross. Although Silva went on to see his first penalty saved, an [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] save against [[Jadon Sancho]] and a miss from [[Jonny Evans]] saw City victorious in the penalty shoot-out. It was the first time since [[2019 FA Community Shield|2019]] that City had won the competition after consecutive defeats in their previous three appearances.<ref name="MM" />

On 12 August, it was announced that Julián Alvarez would be joining [[Atlético Madrid]] for a reported initial fee of £64.4 million with up to £17.1 million in add-ons after two highly successful seasons with City. At the time, this was the highest transfer fee the club had ever received for a player and represented a significant profit for a player acquired for £14 million only two years previously. Alvarez had won the [[Treble (association football)#Continental trebles|continental treble]] in 2023, as well as a [[2022 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] and a [[2024 Copa América|Copa America]] title while a City player.<ref name="JA">{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/czx6kk46d4po |title=Julian Alvarez: Atletico Madrid sign Manchester City striker for £81.5m  |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 August 2024 |access-date=12 August 2024}}</ref>

On 23 August, former captain [[İlkay Gündoğan]] returned to the club on a free transfer, signing a one-year deal after having spent the previous season at Barcelona.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cvge0nre418o |title=Manchester City re-sign Gundogan from Barcelona |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 August 2024 |access-date=23 August 2024 |archive-date=23 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240823101656/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cvge0nre418o |url-status=live}}</ref>

City began their [[2024–25 Premier League|league]] campaign with three strong performances and victories away to Chelsea and [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], and at home to newly promoted [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]]. The games against Ipswich and West Ham United included Haaland's 10th and 11th [[hat-trick]]s since he joined the club, as he became the Premier League player to score the most goals (7) in the first three games of the season.<ref name="HS" /><ref name="MC" /> The Blues led the league over [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on goals scored at the first international break, with both clubs maintaining a 100% record and a goal difference of +7.

On 22 September, City played their first league game of the season against their closest title challengers from the previous two seasons and drew 2–2 at home against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. The first goal was Haaland's 100th for the club in all competitions, achieved in just 105 appearances. This equalled a record set by [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] for the fastest to reach this milestone at a single club. Arsenal were able to come back to take a 2–1 lead by half time, but saw [[Leandro Trossard]] sent off for a second bookable offence shortly before the break. A resolute defensive effort with 10 men and excellent goalkeeping from [[David Raya]] was almost enough to secure the victory and three points for the Gunners, but a scrambled goal from [[John Stones]] in the eighth minute of injury time saved the point for City and ensured they remained unbeaten and at top of the league by a point from Liverpool and [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]].

[[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]] had limped out of the Arsenal match following a collision with [[Thomas Partey]]. On 27 September, it was confirmed that the player had ruptured his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] and would miss the rest of the season in recovery. Guardiola said Rodri was "irreplaceable" during the previous season's title run-in. Rodri missed five games the previous season and City had lost four of them.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-27 |title=Rodri: Manchester City midfielder ruled out for season after ACL surgery |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cp3wlwdkj41o |access-date=2024-10-01 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=2024-09-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240927133116/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp3wlwdkj41o |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Autumn period===
Manchester City remained unbeaten in all competitions up to the October international break. In the Premier League, they were positioned just a point behind Liverpool, securing second place and edging out Arsenal on goal difference. Their form extended to the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], where they held the eighth spot in the new [[Swiss-system tournament|Swiss-style league phase]].

On 7 October, City's legal case against the [[Premier League]] over rules on commercial deals involving club owners concluded with a [[Tribunals in the United Kingdom|tribunal]] ruling. The tribunal upheld two aspects of the club's complaints but rejected others. The case, separate from the ongoing investigation into City's alleged financial breaches, found that shareholder loans should not be excluded from associated party transaction (APT) rules and that some recent rule amendments should not be retained. Both sides claimed partial victory, with City pleased about some rulings and the Premier League relieved that most rules were upheld. The ruling could impact other clubs' compliance with financial regulations.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-07 |title=Man City v Premier League legal case verdict - what does it all mean? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c2lngl47peeo |access-date=2024-10-18 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 14 October, Manchester City's [[Sporting director|director of football]], [[Txiki Begiristain]], announced he would be leaving the club the following June after 12 years, being replaced by [[Sporting CP|Sporting Lisbon]]'s [[Hugo Viana]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 October 2024 |title=Club Statement: Director of Football |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-club-statement-63864262 |website=mancity.com}}</ref>

On 28 October, Rodri became the first current City player to win the prestigious [[Ballon d'Or]] award.<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |date=2024-10-28 |title=Rodri wins 2024 Men's Ballon d'Or |url=https://www.uefa.com/ballondor/news/0292-1c33aa864c69-d47a84004f4d-1000--rodri-wins-2024-men-s-ballon-d-or/ |access-date=2024-11-23 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en |archive-date=2024-11-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241109214949/https://www.uefa.com/ballondor/news/0292-1c33aa864c69-d47a84004f4d-1000--rodri-wins-2024-men-s-ballon-d-or/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

City faced an injury crisis and a series of four consecutive losses before the final international break of the year, marking their worst losing streak since 2006 under [[Stuart Pearce]]. It was also the first time Guardiola had suffered four consecutive defeats in his managerial career. During this period, they were eliminated from the [[EFL Cup]] by [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]] and experienced their first outright Champions League loss in over two years, falling 1–4 to [[Sporting CP|Sporting Lisbon]] in Portugal. Additionally, this streak ended their 10-month and 32-game unbeaten run in the league with away losses to [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] and [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton]], leaving City in second place, trailing Liverpool by five points.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-09 |title=Is Pep Guardiola facing his biggest test at Manchester City? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c079vdd83gzo |access-date=2024-11-10 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=2024-11-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241110103331/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c079vdd83gzo |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 19 November, it was widely reported that Guardiola had extended his contract with the club for a further year to 2026, when he would be able to celebrate the completion of his tenth season at City.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-19 |title=Pep Guardiola: Man City manager agrees one-year contract extension |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cx2lpxkv2gno |access-date=2024-11-23 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=2024-11-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241122150531/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cx2lpxkv2gno |url-status=live}}</ref> Later that week, the club confirmed the extension was for 2 years, until the end of the 2026–27 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pollard |first=Rob |date=21 November 2024 |title=Guardiola signs new City contract! |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pep-guardiola-new-contract-manchester-city-63867814 |access-date=23 November 2024 |website=mancity.com}}</ref>

On 23 November 2024, City lost 0–4 to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] that marked the end of their 52-game unbeaten streak at home. It was the Citizen's first home defeat since November 2022 when [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] claimed a surprise victory at the same venue. Despite having most of the ball possession and creating 23 attempts at goal, City were made to rue wasteful chances while their opponent on the day converted their chances clinically.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-24 |title=Maddison and Spurs end City's 52-game unbeaten home run in style |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/sports/maddison-and-spurs-end-citys-52-game-unbeaten-home-run-style-1000981 |access-date=2024-11-26 |website=The Business Standard |language=en}}</ref>

===Christmas and New Year===
The club's poor run of form continued into December and included further league defeats to Liverpool, Manchester United and Aston Villa; and a comprehensive Champions League defeat away at [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]. At the nadir, City had just one win in thirteen games with nine defeats.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-24 |title=Pep Guardiola: 'Self-doubt, errors and big changes - inside crisis at Man City' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c7vemyd9g50o |access-date=2025-01-18 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-21 |title=Man City lose to Aston Villa: Pep Guardiola says struggling champions 'have to find a way' to win again |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cdd6rl9v953o |access-date=2025-01-18 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

However, their form improved somewhat in the New Year with consecutive victories against West Ham and [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester]] in the league and a comprehensive 8–0 victory against [[2024–25 EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] in the third round of the [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Manchester City 8-0 Salford City: Jack Grealish ends drought in FA Cup romp |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crmngkjg221t |access-date=2025-01-18 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

As the January transfer window opened, it was rumoured that City would be in the market for an additional central defender to cover for the reoccurring injuries to John Stones, [[Rúben Dias]] and [[Nathan Aké]]; an additional defensive midfielder to cover for the long-term injury to Rodri and an additional forward to support Erling Haaland as replacement for [[Julián Alvarez]]. On 11 January, Guardiola revealed that club captain Kyle Walker had requested an immediate transfer away from the club. He subsequently joined [[AC Milan|Milan]] on loan for the remainder of the season, with an option to buy at the end of the season.<ref name="WJ" /> Kevin De Bruyne replaced Walker as club captain.

In January 2025, it was reported that Manchester City had reached an agreement with [[RC Lens]] and [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] to bring [[Abdukodir Khusanov]] and [[Vitor Reis (footballer, born January 2006)|Vitor Reis]] respectively to the [[City of Manchester Stadium]]. The deal for the former was believed to be £33.5 million while the latter £29.6 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=James |first=Alex |date=2025-01-12 |title=Man City ready to unleash £33.5million signing as transfer plan clear |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/man-city-ready-unleash-335million-30760887 |access-date=2025-01-14 |website=Manchester Evening News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Vitor Reis: Man City reach £29.4m agreement in principle to sign 19-year-old Palmeiras defender |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/13288441/vitor-reis-man-city-reach-gbp29-4m-agreement-in-principle-to-sign-19-year-old-palmeiras-defender |access-date=2025-01-14 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> Both deals were confirmed on 20 and 21 January.<ref name="CC" /><ref name="SU" /> It was also rumoured that City had agreed with [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] for the signing of forward [[Omar Marmoush]] on a five-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 January 2025 |title=Omar Marmoush: Manchester City agree deal to sign forward from Eintracht Frankfurt |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11679/13288727/omar-marmoush-manchester-city-agree-deal-to-sign-forward-from-eintracht-frankfurt |access-date=19 January 2025 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref> That transfer was confirmed on 23 January.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pollard |first=Rob |title=City seal signing of Omar Marmoush |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-sign-omar-marmoush-63873209 |access-date=2025-01-28 |website=Manchester City FC |language=en}}</ref>

Consecutive defeats in the Champions League league stage at Juventus and [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint Germain]] had left City unexpectedly on the verge of elimination from the competition. They required a victory in their final league stage game home to [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] to avoid this. On 29 January, City came back from a goal down to win 3–1. However, their final position in the league table at 22nd meant they would have to compete for a place in the last 16 round in a two-legged playoff game against either [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] or defending champions [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. The resulting ties against Madrid meant the two clubs were meeting for the fourth consecutive season in the competition at the knockout stages.<ref name="CL" />

On 2 February, City suffered a comprehensive 1–5 defeat at the [[Emirates Stadium]] to their closest rivals of recent seasons, Arsenal. City had conceded an early goal from a defensive error, but equalised in the 55th minute thanks to Haaland. However, the Gunners went on to quickly score four unanswered goals to delight their fans and close the gap to league leaders Liverpool. The defeat left City in fifth place, two points behind Chelsea.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arsenal v Man City, 2024/25 {{!}} Premier League |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/116057 |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref>

Before the winter transfer window closed the following day, City completed their fourth significant signing of the window, welcoming defensive midfielder [[Nico González (footballer, born 2002)|Nico González]] from [[FC Porto|Porto]] for £50 million.<ref name="FW" />

On 11 February, City were defeated 2–3 In the first leg of their play-off tie at home to Real Madrid. Despite having led twice with goals from Haaland, Madrid were able to equalise with strikes from [[Kylian Mbappé]] and ex-City youth player [[Brahim Díaz]], before [[Jude Bellingham]] scored with virtually the last kick of the match to take a one-goal advantage back home for the second leg the following week; and end City's undefeated home streak in the competition which had stretched to 34 games over more than six seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=Man City vs Real Madrid: UEFA Champions League 2024/25 Knockout play-offs |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2044474--man-city-vs-real-madrid/ |access-date=2025-02-11 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref>

A 4–0 home victory over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] the following weekend provided some hope that team's performances were improving, and that the new players recruited in January were already impressing. The game was notable for a debut hat-trick from Marmoush and an impressive performance from Nico, whom Guardiola later described as a "mini-Rodri".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Manchester City 4-0 Newcastle United: Omar Marmoush hits hat-trick in thumping win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c2k57y0dnnyt |access-date=2025-02-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

However, on 19 February, City suffered a further defeat in Madrid, losing 1–3 on the night through a [[Kylian Mbappé|Mbappé]] hat-trick, and 3–6 on aggregate. This ended City's participation in European competition for the season and was the first time the Blues had failed to reach the last 16 of the Champions League since [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|2012–13]], when they had been knocked out at the group stages.<ref name="RM" />

Defeat at home to runaway league leaders Liverpool followed by victory away to Tottenham Hotspur at the end of February put City back into fourth place and the qualification places for next season's Champions League just a point behind surprise third-placed team [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], and a point ahead of Chelsea in fifth.

===Season run-in===
The FA Cup was now City's only realistic chance of domestic silverware for the season. They faced lower-league opposition in the third, fourth and fifth rounds and duly qualified for the quarter-finals where they were drawn away to Premier League opposition for the first time that season against Bournemouth.

Otherwise, their objective was to secure Champions League qualification in the remaining league fixtures and prepare for the FIFA Club World Cup being held in June.

On 30 March, Manchester City won their FA Cup quarter-final tie against Bournemouth 2–1, coming from behind with both goals assisted by academy graduate [[Nico O'Reilly]] who came on at half-time and played at left-back rather than his usual midfield role. However, the result was marred by an ankle injury picked up by top scorer Erling Haaland, which the club later announced would rule him out for five to seven weeks and possibly the remainder of the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Editorial |first=Man City |title=Injury update: Erling Haaland |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/injury-update-erling-haaland-63879043 |access-date=2025-04-06 |website=Manchester City FC |language=en}}</ref> Nevertheless, City comfortably beat Leicester City 2–0 in their next league fixture with Omar Marmoush playing as the centre forward.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Manchester City 2-0 Leicester City: Jack Grealish scores in comfortable home win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cr727jj4ez9t |access-date=2025-04-06 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 4 April, Kevin De Bruyne announced on his social media that he would be leaving the club at the end of the season after 10 years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-04 |title=Kevin de Bruyne to leave Manchester City at end of season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cj3x0jpmgv4o |access-date=2025-04-06 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> With a record 18 trophies and four Player of the Season awards at that time, he would be considered one of the greatest footballers to have ever played for the club.

On 6 April, the 196th [[Manchester derby]] ended in a 0–0 draw at Old Trafford to leave City in fifth place, one point behind Chelsea and a point ahead of Aston Villa, with Newcastle in seventh, two points behind but with two games in hand.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier League LIVE: Manchester United 0-0 Manchester City - report, score, radio commentary & live text updates |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c2dep9ejpykt#Report |access-date=2025-04-06 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Three consecutive league victories (against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] and Aston Villa) for the first time since October 2024 in April kept City in the race for Champions League qualification.

On 27 April, the Blues beat Nottingham Forest 2–0 at [[Wembley Stadium]] with goals from [[Rico Lewis]] and Joško Gvardiol to qualify for their third consecutive [[2025 FA Cup final|FA Cup final]] where they would meet Crystal Palace.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nottingham Forest 0-2 Man City: Pep Guardiola's side reach FA Cup final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cg72ezz8307t |access-date=2025-04-27 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 17 May, Palace secured their first-ever major trophy with a 1–0 victory over City in the 2025 FA Cup final at Wembley. [[Eberechi Eze]] scored the decisive goal in the 16th minute, finishing a well-crafted [[counterattack]] set up by [[Daniel Muñoz (footballer)|Daniel Muñoz]]. Despite City's dominance in possession, Palace goalkeeper [[Dean Henderson]], who had avoided an early [[Red card (association football)|red card]] when he handled the ball outside his area to thwart a Haaland one-on-one chance, emerged as a hero, saving a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] from Omar Marmoush and making key stops throughout the match. City's frustration grew as they failed to claim major domestic silverware for the first time since the [[2016–17 Manchester City F.C. season|2016–17 season]].<ref name="CF" />

The final home game against [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] on 20 May was notable for a stunning goal of the season from Marmoush, the long-awaited return of Rodri from his injury and the final home appearance of Kevin De Bruyne who was honoured in a presentation after the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Man City 3-1 Bournemouth: Marmoush, Silva and Gonzalez score for hosts |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crmk7lgj7gjt |access-date=2025-05-30 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

A run of 10 unbeaten league games ensured City concluded the 2024–25 Premier League season in third place, securing [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] qualification with a 2–0 victory at [[Fulham F.C|Fulham]] on the final day.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fulham 0-2 Manchester City: Man City seal third place with victory at Fulham |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cjdzzrkd9vgt |access-date=2025-05-30 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> However, their 71 points collected over the season was their worst points haul since [[2015–16 Manchester City F.C. season|2015–16]], and the worst for Pep Guardiola as a manager over a 38-match league season.

===End of season and FIFA Club World Cup===
The revamped [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]] spanned both the official 2024–25 and [[2025–26 Manchester City F.C. season|2025–26]] seasons. The Premier League announced on 27 March that an additional transfer window would open from 1 to 10 June to align with the window announced by FIFA in October 2024 that would permit participants in that competition to make transfers before the competition began.

It had been anticipated that City's squad would need a major overhaul in the summer to remain competitive at the highest level after a trophyless season. While this transition began in the previous January transfer window, further changes were expected, particularly in midfield, at full-back and potentially at centre-half if the club chose to offload some of their aging and injury-prone players. Specifically, City were rumoured to be progressing their interests in left back [[Rayan Aït-Nouri]] from [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]], and midfielders [[Tijjani Reijnders]] from [[AC Milan|Milan]] and [[Rayan Cherki]] from [[FC Lyon|Lyon]] in order to complete these in time for the Club World Cup. City had also previously been linked with an interest in [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] star [[Florian Wirtz]], but had pulled out of negotiations.

These three transfers, and that of back-up goalkeeper [[Marcus Bettinelli]] from Chelsea, were duly completed between 9 and 11 June at a total estimated cost of £112 million.<ref>{{cite news |date=9 June 2025 |title=Rayan Ait Nouri transfer news: Man City complete £36.3m deal for Wolves defender |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/13380667/rayan-ait-nouri-transfer-news-man-city-complete-36-3m-deal-for-wolves-defender#:~:text=Man%20City%20have%20finalised%20a,5.3m%20in%20add%2Dons. |access-date=9 June 2025 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=11 June 2025 |title=Tijjani Reijnders transfer: Man City complete £46.3m deal to sign midfielder from AC Milan on five-year contract |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13379209/tijjani-reijnders-transfer-man-city-complete-46-3m-deal-to-sign-midfielder-from-ac-milan-on-five-year-contract |access-date=11 June 2025 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=10 June 2025 |title=Rayan Cherki: Manchester City complete £34m deal to sign attacking midfielder from Lyon |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11679/13380685/rayan-cherki-manchester-city-complete-34m-deal-to-sign-attacking-midfielder-from-lyon |access-date=10 June 2025 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=10 June 2025 |title=Bettinelli joins City |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/marcus-bettinelli-joins-city-63885155 |access-date=10 June 2025 |publisher=Manchester City FC}}</ref>

On 19 June, Guardiola announced he would be breaking from the tradition of recent seasons and appointing his own club captain and leadership team instead of leaving it to a team vote. He subsequently confirmed that Bernardo Silva would take over the captaincy from De Bruyne, supported by Rodri, Dias, Haaland and Gündogan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marshall |first=Tyrone |date=2025-06-20 |title=Man City have a new captain but the real question is what comes next |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/man-city-new-captain-real-31891599 |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=Manchester Evening News |language=en}}</ref>

Manchester City comfortably won their three group games at the Club World Cup, including an impressive 5–2 victory against Juventus which ensured they would avoid some of the other major European clubs in the knock-out rounds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Juventus vs Man City LIVE: Club World Cup score, team news, stats & updates |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cvg9r4nyqdet |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> However, City went on to exit the competition at the round of 16 stage with a 3–4 [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|a.e.t.]] defeat to [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]].<ref name=":0" />

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 19 March 2024, Manchester City announced they would return to the [[United States]] during pre-season, with matches against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[AC Milan|Milan]], [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] as part of the [[2024 Florida Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=City return to USA for 2024/25 pre-season tour |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-usa-tour-2024-63846442 |access-date=26 March 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=19 March 2024}}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2024–25 FA Cup}}
As a Premier League side, Manchester City entered the FA Cup at the third round stage, and were drawn at home to [[EFL League Two]] side [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]].<ref>{{cite news |title=FA Cup third round proper draw |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2024/dec/02/emirates-fa-cup-third-round-proper-draw-details-2024-25 |access-date=2 December 2024 |publisher=The Football Association |date=2 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=City's FA Cup clash with Salford to be broadcast live |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-v-salford-city-fa-cup-3rd-round-date-and-time-announced-63869077 |access-date=9 December 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=6 December 2024}}</ref> In the fourth round draw, they were handed an away tie against [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]].<ref>{{cite news |title=The Emirates FA Cup fourth round proper draw has been confirmed |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2025/jan/12/emirates-fa-cup-fourth-round-proper-draw-20251201 |access-date=17 January 2025 |publisher=The Football Association |date=12 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Date and kick-off time confirmed for FA Cup trip to Leyton Orient |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/leyton-orient-v-manchester-city-fixture-fate-confirmed-63872727 |access-date=17 January 2025 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=17 January 2025}}</ref> The draw for the fifth round was held on 10 February. City were drawn at home to [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]].<ref>{{cite news |date=10 February 2025 |title=FA Cup fifth-round draw: Manchester City to host Plymouth |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cvgevk5pzvgo |access-date=10 February 2025 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=FA Cup date and kick off time confirmed |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/city-v-plymouth-fa-cup-date-and-kick-off-time-confirmed-63875123 |access-date=14 February 2025 |publisher=Manchester City FC |date=14 February 2025}}</ref> The quarter-final draw was made on 2 March, handing City an away trip to face Premier League side [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]].<ref>{{cite news |title=The draw for the Emirates FA Cup 2024-25 quarter-final has been made |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2025/mar/02/emirates-fa-cup-quarter-final-draw-made-202502043 |access-date=2 March 2025 |publisher=The Football Association |date=2 March 2025}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2024–25 EFL Cup}}
As a Premier League team involved in European competition, Manchester City entered the EFL Cup in the third round, and were drawn at home against [[EFL Championship]] side [[Watford F.C.|Watford]].<ref>{{cite news |date=28 August 2024 |title=City to face Watford in Carabao Cup Round 3 |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-discover-carabao-cup-third-round-opponents-63860473 |access-date=31 August 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C.}}</ref> In the fourth round, they were drawn away to fellow Premier League side [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Draw made for Carabao Cup Round Four |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2024/september/25/draw-made-for-carabao-cup-round-four/ |access-date=26 September 2024 |publisher=English Football League |date=24 September 2024 |archive-date=7 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007175543/https://www.efl.com/news/2024/september/25/draw-made-for-carabao-cup-round-four/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===FA Community Shield===
{{main|2024 FA Community Shield}}
As the defending [[2023–24 Premier League|Premier League]] champions, Manchester City faced reigning [[2023–24 FA Cup|FA Cup]] winners [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the traditional season opener. United previously defeated City in the [[2024 FA Cup final|FA Cup final]] earlier that year.

====Knockout phase====
{{main|2024–25 UEFA Champions League knockout phase}}

=====Knockout phase play-offs=====
By finishing 22nd in the league phase, Manchester City entered the knockout phase play-offs instead of qualifying directly for the round of 16. They were unseeded and would be drawn against one of the sides that finished in 11th or 12th place, namely [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] or [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], respectively. The draw on 31 January confirmed Madrid as their opponents.<ref name="CL">{{cite news |title=Champions League knockout phase play-off draw: Manchester City get Real Madrid, Bayern visit Celtic |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0295-1cf1ef38c981-26fd3e0def66-1000--champions-league-knockout-phase-play-off-draw-manchester-/ |access-date=31 January 2025 |publisher=UEFA |date=31 January 2025}}</ref> The two teams would meet for the fourth consecutive season in the knockout stages.

===FIFA Club World Cup===
{{main|2025 FIFA Club World Cup}}
Manchester City qualified for the revamped tournament as winners of the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League]]. Their opponents were confirmed on 5 December,<ref>{{cite news |title=City discover FIFA Club World Cup 2025 group stage opponents |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/fifa-club-world-cup-2025-group-stage-draw-63869010 |access-date=9 December 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=5 December 2024}} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> with the fixture dates announced two days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=City's FIFA Club World Cup 2025 fixtures confirmed |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/fifa-club-world-cup-2025-fixtures-confirmed-63869011 |access-date=9 December 2024 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=7 December 2024}} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
